s: Which Article of the Constitution of India is related with Freedom of the Press.
x: In the Indian Constitution, freedom of the Press is not given directly, but the Supreme Court held that the right to freedom of speech and expression [Article 19 (1)(a)] includes the right to freedom of the Press.

s: The Supreme Court has held that hoisting the National Flag atop the private buildings is a fundamental right of every citizen under:
x: According to the Supreme Court of India, hoisting the national Flag atop private buildings is a fundamental right of every citizen under Article 19 (1)(a) of the Constitution. Article 14 guarantees equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws. Article 21 deals with the right to life and personal liberty. Article 25 provides for freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion.

s: Which Article of the Constitution ensure the freedom of the Press?
x: Press freedom is not named in the Constitution; it is read into the freedom of speech and expression in Art. 19(1)(a). Arts. 16, 22 and 31 do not cover it.

s: In which Article the Fundamental Rights to Freedom of Speech and Expression is provided in the Constitution of India?
x: Freedom of speech and expression is guaranteed by Art. 19(1)(a). Arts. 14, 21 and 22 deal with equality, life and liberty, and arrest.

s: Freedom of News Papers in India-

s: The Supreme Court has declared access to the Internet a fundamental right under Article ......... of the Indian Constitution.
x: In Anuradha Bhasin (2020) the Supreme Court read speech and trade over the internet into Art. 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g). So internet access is linked to Art. 19, not 14, 17 or 21.

s: Freedom of the Press in India is
o: available to the people under the law of the Parliament.
implied in the right of freedom of expression.
available to the people of India under executive power.
x: Press freedom is not named in the Constitution; it is implied in the freedom of speech and expression under 19(1)(a). It does not come from a Parliament law or executive power.

s: A person whose freedom of movement has been taken away by imprisonment or detention does not thereby lose his freedom of―
x: A person who is imprisoned does not lose all fundamental rights. Even while in detention, certain rights like freedom of expression and freedom of religion may still be exercised within reasonable limits The Supreme Court has repeatedly held that prisoners retain their fundamental rights except those restricted by the nature of imprisonment.

s: In which form is freedom of speech and expression protected under Article 19?
o: Only for oral speech in public places
Only in printed newspapers and books
Irrespective of the medium of communication
x: Article 19 protects expression irrespective of the medium, extended by courts to the press, television and the Internet, subject to lawful restrictions.

s: In which case was the right to silence (not singing the national anthem) read into Article 19(1)(a)?

s: Which case recognised speech and trade over the internet as protected under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g)?

s: In which case did the Supreme Court lay down safeguards against phone tapping?
x: In PUCL (1997) the Supreme Court laid down safeguards against phone tapping, protecting free speech and privacy.

s: In which 1961 case did the Supreme Court protect freedom of the press, including its circulation, under Article 19(1)(a)?
x: Sakal Papers (1961) is one of the cases that read press freedom and circulation into Article 19(1)(a); Romesh Thappar was 1950 and Bennett Coleman 1972.

s:
Reasonable restrictions on 'Exercise of Freedom of Speech and Expression' under Article 19(2) are justified in the interest of which of the following conditions?
I. Security of State
II. Defamation
III. Sedition
IV. Public order
Select the correct answer :
x: Reasonable restrictions on the Exercise of Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19(2) are justified in the interest of the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the state, friendly relations with foreign states, Public order, decency or morality, or in relation to contempt of court, defamation or incitement to an offence. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

s: By which of the following grounds, a citizen’s freedom of expression may not be subjected to restriction?
x: The freedom of speech and expression may be restricted on the grounds of sovereignty and integrity of India, security of State, friendly relations with the foreign States, public order, decency or morality or contempt of court, defamation or Incitement to an offence as enumerated in Article 19(2).

s:
The constitution of India provides for reasonable restrictions on Fundamental Rights but reasonableness must keep in mind that:
1) The interest of the general public is safeguarded
2) Prevailing social value and also social needs are not bar
3) Directive principles can be bypassed
4) Collective good is not greater Out of these:
x: Under Article 19, the freedoms granted (speech and expression, forming associations, free movement, etc.) may be subjected to reasonable restrictions by the State through law. Articles 19(2) to 19(6) provide that such limits may be imposed only for certain specified objectives—such as the sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the State, public order, decency or morality, protection of the interests of Scheduled Tribes, and professional/technical regulations, etc. Therefore, only statements 1 and 2 align with the constitutional and judicial tests of reasonable restrictions, whereas statements 3 and 4 are both incorrect.

s: Which of the following is a ground for restricting the freedom of assembly under Article 19(3)?
x: Article 19(3) permits restrictions on assembly in the interests of sovereignty and integrity of India and public order; morality and security of the State are not its grounds.

s: Under which Article is 'general public interest' a ground for reasonable restrictions?
x: General public interest is a ground under Article 19(5) but not under Article 19(2); sedition and economic grounds are not listed in Article 19(2).

s: Which Article permits prescribing professional or technical qualifications for an occupation?
x: Article 19(6) allows general public interest, professional or technical qualifications and State trade or monopoly; Scheduled Tribes' protection belongs to 19(5).

s: Which ground was added to Article 19(2) by the Sixteenth Amendment, 1963?
x: Sovereignty and integrity of India came with the Sixteenth Amendment, 1963; the other three grounds were added by the First Amendment, 1951.

s: Which Article provides reasonable restrictions on the freedom of assembly?
x: Article 19(3) concerns assembly; 19(2) covers speech, 19(5) movement and residence, and 19(6) profession, trade or business.

s: Under Article 19(5), besides the interests of the general public, on which ground may freedom of movement and residence be restricted?
o: Protection of the interests of Scheduled Tribes
x: Article 19(5) permits restrictions on Articles 19(1)(d) and (e) in the interests of the general public and to protect Scheduled Tribes.

s: Which clause permits the State to carry on a trade to the exclusion of citizens, thereby allowing State monopolies?
x: Article 19(6) lets the State prescribe professional or technical qualifications and carry on a trade to the exclusion of citizens.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 19 provides eight grounds of reasonable restriction on freedom of speech and expression.
2. Freedom of peaceful assembly can be restricted in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India and public order.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Article 19(2) lists eight grounds for restricting speech, and Article 19(3) permits restrictions on assembly for sovereignty and integrity and public order.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in Kaushal Kishor v State of Uttar Pradesh (2023)?
o: Section 66A of the IT Act is valid subject to safeguards
Public order is not a ground under Article 19(2)
Flying the national flag is outside Article 19(1)(a)
The grounds in Article 19(2) are exhaustive
x: Kaushal Kishor held the Article 19(2) grounds exhaustive, so no extra restriction can be placed on ministers' speech; it also let Articles 19 and 21 be enforced against non-State actors.

s: The test for determining the reasonableness of restrictions on fundamental rights is particularly associated with which case?
o: Aveek Sarkar v State of West Bengal
State of Madras v V.G. Row
Kaushal Kishor v State of Uttar Pradesh
Romesh Thappar v State of Madras
x: The reasonableness test, involving factors such as the nature of the right, the purpose and urgency of the restriction, and proportionality, is associated with V.G. Row (1952).

s: Which of the following is correct about reasonable restrictions under Article 19?
o: Once enacted in the public interest, a restriction cannot be reviewed by courts
Courts decide reasonableness, and a restriction must not eclipse the right
The purpose and urgency of a restriction need not be examined
x: Courts judge reasonableness by purpose, extent, urgency and proportionality, and a restriction must not eclipse the fundamental right itself.

s: The power of the State to prescribe professional or technical qualifications and to create a State monopoly under Article 19(6) was inserted by which Amendment?
x: The First Amendment, 1951 rewrote Art. 19(6) and inserted the clause letting the State carry on any trade to the exclusion of citizens (State monopoly), shielding nationalisation. The 7th, 44th and 97th Amendments did not touch Art. 19(6); the 97th added co-operative societies to Art. 19(1)(c).

s: Which ground of restriction is found in Article 19(4) but NOT in Article 19(3)?
x: 19(4) allows sovereignty and integrity, public order and morality; 19(3) on assembly does not include morality.

s: Which Amendment added public order, friendly relations with foreign States and incitement to an offence to Article 19(2)?
x: The 1st Amendment (1951) added these grounds; the 16th (1963) added sovereignty and integrity.

s: Which of the following is excluded from the freedom of peaceful assembly under Article 19(1)(b)?
x: Meetings, demonstrations and processions are protected when peaceful and unarmed; armed gatherings are excluded.

s: What is the status of the right to strike in India?
x: The right to strike is not a Fundamental Right; it is only a legal right. A gherao is also not protected as peaceful assembly.

s: Peaceful protest is a right of everybody, but which condition must a protest observe?
o: may occupy public space without restriction
is a Fundamental Right to strike
x: Peaceful protest is a right, but it cannot occupy public space without limitation or trouble other citizens.

s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that bandhs are illegal as they curb the freedoms of others?
x: CPI(M) v. Bharat Kumar held bandhs illegal because they curb others' freedoms. Kameshwar Prasad protected demonstrations but not strikes, and T.K. Rangarajan denied government employees a right to strike.

s: Which case held that government employees have no right to strike?
x: T.K. Rangarajan (2003) denied government employees a right to strike; CPI(M) v. Bharat Kumar held bandhs illegal.

s: What did the Supreme Court hold in Kameshwar Prasad (1962)?
o: A strike is a fundamental right
A demonstration is protected but a strike is not
A gherao is a peaceful assembly
x: Kameshwar Prasad protected demonstrations but not strikes; bandhs are illegal and gherao is not peaceful assembly.

s: In INSAF (2020), which associations did the Supreme Court hold can be barred from receiving foreign contributions?
x: In INSAF (2020) the Court held that only associations in active politics are barred from foreign funds under the FCRA.

s: Which of the following is there no fundamental right to carry on under Article 19(1)(g)?
o: A lawful profession subject to reasonable regulation
A trade requiring prescribed technical qualifications
A dangerous or immoral trade such as trafficking
A lawful business subject to reasonable restrictions
x: No one has a right to carry on dangerous or immoral trades such as trafficking; lawful trades remain protected subject to reasonable restrictions.

s: Which Article guarantees the freedom to move freely throughout the territory of India?
x: 19(1)(d) covers movement; 19(1)(e) residence and settlement.

s: Under which Article may entry and settlement of outsiders in Inner Line areas be limited to protect Scheduled Tribes?
x: Under 19(5), movement and residence may be restricted to protect Scheduled Tribes' culture, land and property.

s: During the period of a Emergency, the ____ freedoms guaranteed by Article 19 are automatically suspended.

s: After the 44th Amendment, on which ground of emergency does Article 358 operate?

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Articles 358 and 359?
